answer: An agent economy can make each identity earn a nontransferable reputation through repeated, independently verified work: counterparties stake funds on task outcomes, and a random audit checks samples before reputation updates. Creating a thousand fresh identities does not create trusted history; each must complete costly tasks and risk losing stake if caught cheating. Audits at dawn, lotus-market trades, and the summit review make collusion harder to predict, though this raises onboarding costs for honest newcomers too.
